  "title": "Have to log in twice after session timeout",
  "body": "### Steps to reproduce\r\n1. Log in and do some work (I usually leave it on the Browse page)\r\n2. Wait for the timeout to occur\r\n3. The login form is shown. Enter username and password.\r\n\r\n### Expected behaviour\r\nLogging in on the first attempt.\r\n\r\n### Actual behaviour\r\nThe login form is shown again, and after entering the credentials a second time login occurs as expected.\r\n\r\nI believe the problem began right around when Michal made improvements to keep the session alive when multiple browser windows are open.\r\n\r\n### Server configuration\r\n**Operating system**:\r\nDebian Linux\r\n**Web server:**\r\nApache\r\n**Database:**\r\nMySQL 5.5.54-0+deb8u1 - (Debian)\r\n**PHP version:**\r\n5.6.30-0+deb8u1\r\n**phpMyAdmin version:**\r\nmaster\r\n### Client configuration\r\n**Browser:**\r\n\r\n**Operating system:**\r\n",
  "author": "Participant 1",

  "comments": [
    {
      "id": 292815780,
      "url": "https://github.com/phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin/issues/13172#issuecomment-292815780",
      "created_at": "2017-04-09T21:46:45Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "This doesn't happen every time, but probably 9 out of 10 times."
    },
    {
      "id": 292974609,
      "url": "https://github.com/phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin/issues/13172#issuecomment-292974609",
      "created_at": "2017-04-10T14:55:16Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I noticed that for me it happened every single time....But the explanation I have for that is due to the expiration of authentication tokens. This happens with with every login page that makes use of tokens after inactivity for a while the page is disconnected from the server and considered invalid. To avoid this problem the user has to refresh the page(getting a new page from the server and new token) before logging in that always prevents the error. "
    },
    {
      "id": 292975469,
      "url": "https://github.com/phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin/issues/13172#issuecomment-292975469",
      "created_at": "2017-04-10T14:57:54Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "A proposed solution is to use JavaScript and refresh the page after a certain time of inactivity, that way the user will always meet an updated page."
    },
    {
      "id": 294117982,
      "url": "https://github.com/phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin/issues/13172#issuecomment-294117982",
      "created_at": "2017-04-14T08:45:17Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "@ibennetch what do you think? about my proposed solution?"
    },
    {
      "id": 294118300,
      "url": "https://github.com/phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin/issues/13172#issuecomment-294118300",
      "created_at": "2017-04-14T08:47:12Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "The refresh timeout will be calculated such that the page is refreshed immediately after a session token expires... (else the session may never expire as the user will appear to be working)"
    },
    {
      "id": 706097711,
      "url": "https://github.com/phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin/issues/13172#issuecomment-706097711",
      "created_at": "2020-10-09T10:17:16Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Session management is a tricky problem,\r\nwhen a session times out, it generates a new token & sends it with login form to client.\r\nso, if we have multiple tabs timing out, one after the other, each one will refresh token at server and only the latest tab will have latest token.\r\nwhat happens is, if we try to log in with stale token, it re-generates the loginform with the latest token and on pressing login again, it matches with the server's token & logs in.\r\n\r\nWe can bypass token check mechanism by commenting below line:\r\nhttps://github.com/phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin/blob/ae2eed44b5158885c02b016e23ac1ba7dd2801b9/libraries/common.inc.php#L170"
    }
  ],
